concept.name: Dimensional Modeling & Star Schemas

relationships.description: Connects Dimensional Modeling & Star Schemas to data warehousing lakehouse in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Dimensional modeling (Kimball methodology) organizes analytical data into numeric **Fact tables** surrounded by descriptive **Dimension tables** (Star Schema), optimizing for fast BI aggregations, clear business grain, and historical accuracy via Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD).
spark.keyTakeaway: Declare the exact grain of every fact table first—one row per order line, per click, or per daily snapshot—before adding a single metric or dimension key.

concept.whyItMatters: Querying normalized 3NF OLTP tables directly for analytics forces 8-way joins, produces double-counted revenue when 1-to-many tables fan out, and breaks historical reports whenever a customer changes tier or a product changes category.
whenToUse: Building enterprise data warehouses and lakehouses in Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or Databricks SQL using dbt for BI dashboards (Tableau, Looker, Power BI).
Modeling business processes—orders, payments, ad impressions, warehouse inventory—where analysts slice additive metrics (`revenue`, `qty`) by conformed attributes (`date`, `region`, `product`).
Preserving point-in-time historical truth (e.g., what territory a sales rep belonged to when a deal closed last quarter) via SCD Type 2.
whenNotToUse: OLTP transactional workloads requiring high-concurrency row-level `INSERT`/`UPDATE` with strict foreign-key normalization (use 3NF).
Semi-structured log exploration or ad-hoc ML feature-store prototyping where raw JSON/Parquet event streams suffice before schema stabilization.
Pure graph traversal workloads (fraud rings, social networks) where multi-hop recursive joins belong in a graph engine.
keyPoints: Every fact table must have an explicit, unambiguous **grain** (e.g., 'one row per checkout line item'); mixing grains in one table causes silent double-counting.
Star schemas denormalize dimension hierarchies into flat, wide tables (`dim_product` holds category, brand, and department) to minimize joins, unlike Snowflake schemas that normalize dimensions.
**Surrogate keys** (hashed or sequential integers, e.g., `dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key`) decouple warehouse joins from mutable source-system natural keys and support SCD Type 2 versioning.
**Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)**: Type 1 overwrites history; Type 2 inserts a new versioned row with `valid_from`, `valid_to`, and `is_current` to preserve historical context.

Facts come in three types: **Transaction** (one row per event), **Periodic Snapshot** (daily account balances), and **Accumulating Snapshot** (order lifecycle milestones: ordered -> shipped -> delivered).

examples.title: E-Commerce Star Schema in BigQuery + dbt
examples.scenario: A retail analytics team migrates 14 normalized MySQL tables (`orders`, `order_items`, `skus`, `categories`, `brands`, `users`) into a Kimball Star Schema.
examples.outcome: Creating `fct_order_items` (grain: 1 row per SKU per order) joined to `dim_product`, `dim_customer` (SCD Type 2), and `dim_date` cuts Looker dashboard p95 query time from 18s to 1.4s and eliminates fan-out revenue bugs.

examples.title: Accumulating Snapshot for Fulfillment SLA Tracking
examples.scenario: Operations needs to measure `order_to_ship_hours` and `ship_to_deliver_hours` across 5M monthly shipments.
examples.outcome: `fct_order_fulfillment` (1 row per order) stores milestone timestamps (`ordered_at`, `packed_at`, `shipped_at`, `delivered_at`) and precomputed lag durations, updated incrementally via dbt `merge`.

tradeOffs.factor: Star Schema (Denormalized Dims) vs. Snowflake Schema (Normalized Dims)
tradeOffs.pro: Star schemas require only 1-hop joins from fact to dimension, making SQL intuitive for analysts and fast for columnar engines.
tradeOffs.con: Repeats parent attributes (e.g., `category_name` repeated across 10k SKU rows), slightly increasing dimension storage.

tradeOffs.factor: SCD Type 2 (Full History) vs. SCD Type 1 (Overwrite)
tradeOffs.pro: Preserves exact historical accuracy when customers move tiers or stores change regions.
tradeOffs.con: Complicates SQL joins (requires `is_current = true` for latest view or `BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to` for as-of joins) and grows dimension row counts.

tradeOffs.factor: Pre-Joined One Big Table (OBT) vs. Star Schema
tradeOffs.pro: OBT avoids runtime joins entirely, speeding up some BI tools on Parquet/BigQuery.
tradeOffs.con: Updating a single customer attribute requires rewriting billions of historical fact rows; conformed dimensions across multiple facts become hard to keep consistent.

failureModes.name: Join Fan-Out & Double-Counting
failureModes.description: Joining a header-level fact (`fct_orders`, `order_total`) directly to a line-level table or an un-filtered SCD2 dimension duplicates `order_total` across multiple rows.
failureModes.mitigation: Model facts at the lowest atomic grain (`fct_order_items`), enforce `unique` + `not_null` dbt tests on surrogate keys, and ensure SCD2 joins match a single version.

failureModes.name: Missing Late-Arriving Dimension Keys (Orphan Facts)
failureModes.description: An order event arrives in Kafka/Snowflake before the new `customer_id` lands in `dim_customer`, causing `INNER JOIN` reports to silently drop revenue.
failureModes.mitigation: Use `LEFT JOIN` in BI semantic layers and map unresolved natural keys to a `-1` ('Unknown / Late Arriving') surrogate row that is backfilled later.

failureModes.name: Non-Additive Metrics Summed Blindly
failureModes.description: Analysts `SUM(account_balance)` across 30 days in a Periodic Snapshot fact table, inflating balances by 30x.
failureModes.mitigation: Document semi-additive measures (`balance`, `inventory_on_hand`) in the semantic layer (LookML / dbt MetricFlow) to aggregate via `LAST_VALUE` over time and `SUM` over other dimensions.

failureModes.name: Overlapping SCD Type 2 Validity Windows
failureModes.description: Out-of-order CDC events create two rows for the same `customer_id` with overlapping `[valid_from, valid_to)` ranges, multiplying downstream joins.
failureModes.mitigation: Use `dbt snapshot` or deterministic `MERGE` with `LEAD(updated_at)` windowing and add a CI test checking for zero overlapping intervals.

commonMistakes: Putting order-header shipping fees on every `fct_order_items` row without allocating them, causing `SUM(shipping_fee)` to multiply by item count.
Using raw mutable source IDs (`email`, `sku_code`) as warehouse join keys instead of stable surrogate keys.
Leaving `NULL` foreign keys in fact tables instead of pointing missing dimensions to a `-1` Unknown row.
Skipping a dedicated `dim_date` table (with fiscal quarters, Indian/US holidays, and weekend flags) and forcing analysts to rewrite date math in every dashboard.
Building un-conformed duplicate dimensions (`dim_user_marketing` vs `dim_customer_finance`) with conflicting definitions of 'active user'.

sections.content:
## The idea

**Dimensional modeling**, formalized by Ralph Kimball, structures analytical warehouses around how the business measures processes rather than how transactional apps store state. Numerical measurements live in narrow, long **Fact tables** at a single declared grain, while textual context (`who, what, where, when, why`) lives in wide, denormalized **Dimension tables**. Because every fact references shared **Conformed Dimensions** via surrogate keys, teams can drill across Orders, Returns, and Support Tickets consistently without multi-hop 3NF joins.

## Concrete walkthrough

Design a Star Schema for an online marketplace in Snowflake/BigQuery using dbt:

1. **Declare Grain**: `fct_order_items` = **1 row per `order_item_id`** (atomic line-item grain).
2. **Build Conformed Dimensions**:
   - `dim_date` (`date_key` `YYYYMMDD`, `fiscal_quarter`, `is_holiday`).
   - `dim_product` (`product_sk`, `sku_id`, `product_name`, `category`, `brand`—flattened from 3 normalized tables).
   - `dim_customer` (SCD Type 2 via `dbt snapshot`: `customer_sk`, `customer_id`, `loyalty_tier`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `is_current`).
3. **Populate Fact**: Join staging `stg_order_items` to `dim_customer` where `order_ts >= valid_from AND order_ts < coalesce(valid_to, '9999-12-31')` to lock in the customer's tier *at purchase time*.
4. **Query**: BI tools run `SELECT d.fiscal_quarter, p.category, SUM(f.net_revenue) FROM fct_order_items f JOIN dim_date d ... JOIN dim_product p ... GROUP BY 1, 2`—partitioned by `date_key` and clustered by `product_sk`.

sections.content:
## Fact table types and additivity

Choosing the right fact pattern prevents metric bugs:

- **Transaction Fact** (`fct_order_items`, `fct_payments`): Measures are **fully additive** across all dimensions (`SUM(amount)` works over time, store, and product).
- **Periodic Snapshot** (`fct_daily_inventory`, `fct_daily_account_balance`): One row per entity per period. Measures like `on_hand_qty` are **semi-additive**—you can `SUM` across warehouses on a single day, but NEVER across days (use `AVG` or `LAST_VALUE`).
- **Accumulating Snapshot** (`fct_shipment_lifecycle`): One row per workflow instance, updated as milestones occur. Ideal for funnel conversion and SLA lag durations (`packed_at - ordered_at`).

## Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) strategies

| SCD Type | Mechanism | Historical Accuracy | Storage & Join Complexity | Typical Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Type 0** | Never update after insert | Original value frozen | Minimal | `original_signup_date`, birth date |
| **Type 1** | Overwrite attribute in place | None (old state lost) | Low (1 row per entity) | Fixing typos, `email`, current phone |
| **Type 2** | Insert new row + `valid_from`/`valid_to` | Full point-in-time history | Medium (`is_current` or range join) | Customer `loyalty_tier`, sales `territory` |
| **Type 3** | Add `previous_value` column | Only current + 1 prior state | Low (fixed columns) | Year-over-year org re-alignment comparison |
| **Type 6** | Hybrid (Type 1 + 2 + 3) | Both as-was and current views | High | Enterprise finance needing both historical & restated views |

## Failure modes

- **Mixed-Grain Fact Tables**: Storing both order-level `shipping_cost` and item-level `item_price` in one table causes BI users to sum `shipping_cost` once per item. Either allocate shipping proportionally to items or keep a separate `fct_orders` header table.
- **Dimension Explosion from High-Cardinality Columns**: Putting `user_agent` or raw `timestamp` inside `dim_customer` (SCD2) creates a new row on every click. Keep high-cardinality transient attributes in a separate junk/session dimension or on the fact.
- **Slow Partition Scans in Lakehouses**: Partitioning `fct_order_items` by `customer_sk` instead of `date_key` forces full-table scans on date-filtered dashboards. Always partition by date and Z-order/cluster by high-selectivity foreign keys (`product_sk`, `tenant_id`).
- **Broken Conformed Dimensions**: When Marketing builds `dim_customer` differently from Finance, executive KPIs diverge by 5–10%.

## Modern lakehouse considerations (dbt, Parquet, Iceberg)

Columnar engines (BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB, Spark/Iceberg) compress repeated string values via dictionary and RLE encoding, making Star Schema's denormalized dimensions virtually free in storage. In **dbt**, model staging (`stg_`) -> intermediate (`int_`) -> marts (`fct_`, `dim_`), generate deterministic MD5/SHA256 surrogate keys, and materialize large facts as `incremental` tables (`merge` or `insert_overwrite` on `date_key`) with `unique` and `relationships` schema tests running on every PR.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Write down the exact grain of every fact table in its dbt `schema.yml` description before coding SQL.
- [ ] Test primary surrogate keys for `unique` + `not_null`, and foreign keys for `relationships` (or `-1` Unknown fallback).
- [ ] Partition large fact tables by `date_key` and cluster/Z-order by top filter dimensions.
- [ ] Tag semi-additive and non-additive measures (ratios, balances) in the semantic layer so BI tools never `SUM` them over time.
- [ ] Use `dbt snapshot` (or tested `MERGE` logic) for SCD Type 2 dimensions and assert zero overlapping `[valid_from, valid_to)` intervals.

interviewProblems.title: Dimensional Modeling & Star Schemas
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Dimensional Modeling & Star Schemas. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Dimensional modeling (Kimball methodology) organizes analytical data into numeric **Fact tables** surrounded by descriptive **Dimension tables** (Star Schema), optimizing for fast BI aggregations, clear business grain, and historical accuracy via Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD).

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: fct_order_items applies the primary invariant and coordinates with dim_product.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, dim_product experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Model facts at the lowest atomic grain (`fct_order_items`), enforce `unique` + `not_null` dbt tests on surrogate keys, and ensure SCD2 joins match a single version.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Declare the exact grain of every fact table first—one row per order line, per click, or per daily snapshot—before adding a single metric or dimension key.
Avoid trap: Putting order-header shipping fees on every `fct_order_items` row without allocating them, causing `SUM(shipping_fee)` to multiply by item count.
Avoid trap: Using raw mutable source IDs (`email`, `sku_code`) as warehouse join keys instead of stable surrogate keys.
When to reach for it: Building enterprise data warehouses and lakehouses in Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or Databricks SQL using dbt for BI dashboards (Tableau, Looker, Power BI).

When to reach for it: Modeling business processes—orders, payments, ad impressions, warehouse inventory—where analysts slice additive metrics (`revenue`, `qty`) by conformed attributes (`date`, `region`, `product`).

putItTogether.title: Putting Dimensional Modeling Together
putItTogether.summary: Declare the exact grain of every fact table first—one row per order line, per click, or per daily snapshot—before adding a single metric or dimension key.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Dimensional Modeling before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Creating `fct_order_items` (grain: 1 row per SKU per order) joined to `dim_product`, `dim_customer` (SCD Type 2), and `dim_date` cuts Looker dashboard p95 query time from 18s to 1.4s and eliminates fan-out revenue bugs.
